analysis.investment_thesis: Alivus is a high-quality API manufacturer with strong margins (31% operating) and decent ROIC (~23%), but at an earnings yield of only ~5% (EBIT 657 Cr / EV ~13,114 Cr), it fails the Magic Formula's cheapness test. Growth has stalled at ~4% CAGR over the last 3 years (2022–2025), making the 37x P/E unjustifiable under a systematic value framework.
key_strengths: High-quality API business: 31.45% operating margin and ROCE of 23.3% sustained across multiple years
Nearly debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02) with 74.87% promoter skin-in-the-game via Nirma
Diversified global revenue base across cardiovascular, CNS, diabetes, and oncology APIs
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~5% (EBIT 657 Cr / EV 13,114 Cr) is well below the 6–12% Magic Formula buy threshold
Revenue growth has severely decelerated: only ~4% CAGR from 2022–2025 vs. 17.6% 6-year CAGR, exposing prior optionality assumptions
Massive investing outflow of -616 Cr in FY2025 (vs. avg -128 Cr prior 3 years) with cash dropping from 301 to 71 Cr — capital deployment risk unclear
red_flags: FY2025 investing CF of -616 Cr is 4–5x normal — possible large acquisition/capex unaccounted for in current earnings
FCF declining trend: 465 Cr (2022) → 143 Cr (2023) → 285 Cr (2024) → 225 Cr (2025) — conversion deteriorating
Recent 3-year net profit CAGR of ~5% (419→486 Cr) does not support a 37x P/E multiple
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Alivus: Earnings Yield = EBIT 657 Cr / EV ~13,114 Cr = **5.0%** — below my 6% floor and well under the attractive 12%+ threshold. Return on Capital (proxied by ROCE) = **23.3%** — respectable, clearing the 20% bar. The business earns good returns; the problem is you're paying a full price for it. At EV/EBITDA of 16x and P/E of 37x, the market has priced in a growth story that the recent numbers don't support. From 2022 to 2025, revenue compounded at a mere 3.9% annually — API pricing pressure and competition from Chinese generics appear to be capping the ceiling.

The FY2025 investing outflow of -616 Cr is the single most important data point to investigate: it's a structural break from the -116 to -147 Cr range of prior years, and cash collapsed from 301 Cr to 71 Cr in one year. This could be a strategic acquisition (potentially value-creating) or an ill-timed capex expansion into a low-growth environment. Until clarity emerges, this introduces meaningful capital allocation risk. The forward P/E of 21x suggests either a material earnings step-up is expected or management has guided optimistically — either way, the Magic Formula says: **good business, wrong price**.
